newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-TAYLOR OPTIMISTIC AS TEAM FACE UNFAMILIAR TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR OPTIMISTIC AS TEAM FACE UNFAMILIAR TEST.

text.p: Only one member of Mark Taylor's squad has played a test in India but the Australian captain is optimistic of success in the major game of their six-week tour which opens this weekend.
Australia's schedule includes a one-off test against India and a triangular limited overs series also involving the host couontry and South Africa.

Taylor, who leads a 14-man party, said: "We have players who have played more than 50 tests and yet there is only one amongst us, Steve Waugh, who has played in a test match in India before. It means when we play at Delhi next week, 10 of us will be making our first test appearance in India.

Though optimistic about his side's prospects, Taylor said: "We are not taking things easy as the Indians today are a very strong batting side and on their home wickets their bowlers, too, will be a different proposition."
The Australians leave for the northern town of Patiala on Friday for a three-day opening tour match against the Cricket Board President's XI starting on Saturday.
Taylor said he would have liked two three-day games before the solitary test starting in New Delhi on October 10.
"Perhaps, these days, it is not possible to spend so much time touring," he said. "We came early to put an edge into our form."

Taylor is without leg-spinner Shane Warne and paceman Craig McDermott, though his absence would not be so keenly felt "as in Glenn McGrath we have a prominent strike bowler, who has done so well in the last year. Damien Fleming, too, is coming up well".
Taylor said Warne had not yet recovered from minor surgery on a finger injury.
He said the tour of India would be good preparation ahead of the challenge his side faced from the West Indies at home later in the 1996-97 season.

"(India's captain) Sachin (Tendulkar) is a very affable fellow and gets along very well with our guys. But when he is on the field, he is a different chap altogether. He is a highly competent cricketer and now I understand he is also captaining the side well," Taylor said.
"I think we will have a good, competitive test match, played in the right spirit."
